entities.name: Andronikos Komnenos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Andronikos Komnenos, Latinized as Andronicus Comnenus, was a Byzantine prince of the Komnenian dynasty who played a crucial role in the Fourth Crusade.

Born in the late 11th century, Andronikos Komnenos was the youngest son of Emperor Alexios III Angelos and was raised at the imperial court. His family's influence and connections helped him secure a place among the powerful nobles of the Byzantine Empire.

In 1142, Andronikos Komnenos was implicated in a plot to overthrow his uncle, Emperor John II Komnenos, and was subsequently executed.

Andronikos Komnenos' legacy is marked by his involvement in the devastating Fourth Crusade, which had a profound impact on the Byzantine Empire and the Mediterranean world.

A striking testament to his influence can be seen in the aftermath of the Fourth Crusade, where the Latin Empire was established in Constantinople, marking a significant turning point in the history of the Byzantine Empire.
